purpose: Teach: 鯖/潤/絶大/ホイール/鳴り/マキ/飛ばす/ゾンビ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔、田舎で、鯖の干物、よく、食べたよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本当に、美味かったよな、新鮮で、お互いに、覚えてるかな、ね、二人で。
lines.en: You remember, don't you? Back in the countryside, we used to eat dried mackerel all the time. It was so fresh, so good.
lines.style: Soft, drifting nostalgia. Pauses between thoughts like his mind is reaching back. Gentle cadence, no rush. Warmth wrapped in the memory itself.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。年を取ると、お肌の潤い、なくなってくるわよね、あなた、お互いに、保湿、しっかり、しましょうね、本当に、健康、第一にしましょう。
lines.en: Mm. You know, when you get older, your skin loses its moisture. We should both take care of that—keep up with moisturizing. Health first, really.
lines.style: Warm and slightly distant, like she's talking while thinking of something else. Matter-of-fact but caring underneath. A light singsong rise near 'health first'—speaking a familiar truth.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業者として、私の権限、絶大だった時代、若い頃の話だぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?今は、もう、楽になったわよね、二人で、ゆっくり、暮らせて。
lines.en: When I was younger, back when I was the founder, I had so much authority. Do you remember those days? But now... it's easier. We can just live quietly together.
lines.style: A touch wistful on 'younger' and 'founder'—pride in it but time has weathered it. Slight lift on the question. Then a gentle settling as he arrives at 'easier,' like relief.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お祖父ちゃんの車のホイール、いつも、ピカピカ、磨いてたわよね、覚えてる、あなた、本当に、車、大事にしていたわよね、本当に。
lines.en: When you were young, you used to polish the wheels on your grandfather's car all the time. I remember. You took such good care of it.
lines.style: Watching him across time. Tender but matter-of-fact, like stating something small and true. A slight warm emphasis on 'took care'—noticing his devotion even then.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔、お祭りの太鼓、鳴り響いて、子供たち、ワクワクしたよな、ばあさん、覚えてる、私たちも、楽しかったよな、二人で、よく、お祭り、行ったよな、本当に。
lines.en: At the festivals back then, the drum would echo out and the children would get so excited. You remember, don't you? We had fun too. We went to so many festivals together.
lines.style: Voice softens into the memory of the music. Breath carries the excitement. Slight upward lilt on 'festivals'—he's almost there, hearing it again. Trailing off gently at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 息子の幼馴染、マキちゃんって、いう子、いたわよね、あなた、覚えてる?今、どうしてるのかしらね、ふと、思い出したのよ、私、最近。
lines.en: Remember our son's childhood friend, Maki? I was just thinking about her the other day—wondering how she's doing now.
lines.style: A sudden small thought, like something surfaced. Quiet curiosity. Her tone shifts slightly—less rehearsed, more genuinely wondering. A small thoughtful pause before 'how she's doing.'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、車で、二人で、夜の高速を、飛ばす感覚、本当に、爽快だったよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?今は、もう、できないわよな、お互いに、年だしね。
lines.en: When we were young, driving fast on the highway at night with you—that feeling was so thrilling. You remember, don't you? We can't do that anymore. We're getting old.
lines.style: A small thrill of remembering that speed, that freedom. Then the tempo drops as reality settles in. Not sad—just matter-of-fact. A quiet acceptance in the voice by the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 最近のドラマ、ゾンビが、出てくるものが、増えたわよね、あなた、私、ちょっと、苦手なのよ、本当に、若い人の、好み、変わったわよね、ね、本当に。
lines.en: These days, there are so many dramas with zombies in them. I'm not really into that sort of thing, you know. Young people's tastes have really changed, haven't they?
lines.style: Slightly bemused, a touch wry. Speaking as someone observing from outside. A little shrug in the voice. Warm but gently teasing—like she's both puzzled and forgiving about it.
